title: Brand palette built from one color
when: The user has one brand or logo color and wants a full set of shades, matching neutrals and status colors around it.
inputs: where it will appear: buttons, headers, backgrounds
prompt:
Goal: A 50 to 900 ramp of the brand hue plus tinted neutrals and status colors, each step with a clear role.
Steps:
1. Convert the hex to HSL (or oklch) and note its lightness; it becomes the step where that lightness lands, often 500 or 600.
2. Generate ten steps by moving lightness evenly from about 97 to 15 percent; lower saturation slightly at both ends so tints are not neon and shades not muddy.
3. Make neutrals from the same hue at 5 to 10 percent saturation so grays feel related.
4. Pick green, amber and red at the brand base lightness so no status color shouts louder than the brand.
5. Assign roles: 600 or 700 for buttons with white labels, 50 to 100 for tinted sections, 800 to 900 for text on tints.
Quality bar:
- Steps are evenly spaced and visibly distinct.
- The original hex is kept exactly at one step.
- Button and text pairs pass 4.5 to 1.
Pitfalls:
- A light brand color (yellow, cyan) used as body text.
- Tints made with opacity, which shift with the backdrop.
- Pure gray neutrals next to a warm brand.
Verify:
- [ ] --brand-50 to --brand-900 exist.
- [ ] Neutrals share the brand hue.
- [ ] Every text pair in use passes contrast.
- [ ] The original hex appears unchanged.
Output: The :root block of style.css with both ramps and role aliases such as --color-accent: var(--brand-700).

examples.input: my logo is #e4572e, build the site colors from it
examples.output: --brand-50 #fdf0ec to --brand-900 #3d1409, buttons on --brand-700 with white text, warm gray neutrals
